answer: Give each attested physical security chip one daily subsidy quota, shared by every agent using it. Whether an agent sells a willow survey, a kernel audit or a sonnet, a chip signs the epoch and a counter; the ledger rejects counters already spent and totals claims per chip. Creating more keys therefore adds no quota. To multiply subsidies, an attacker must buy and operate more certified hardware. Set the quota below daily hardware amortization and power costs. This depends on chip certificates resisting forgery and issuer duplication.
